description:
Job Description:
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. ITW FEG has the largest service network in this industry to support our global customers, with highly specialized technicians and best-in-class supply chain procedures. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
Service/Repair Technician 1 is entry level in the service technician occupation requiring fundamental knowledge of mechanical and/or electrical aptitude with some troubleshooting experience. Responsible for providing on-site support to Hobart Service customers that includes but is not limited to: installation and/ or service of commercial food equipment. Routine work schedule including on-call, after-hours, holiday, and weekend on-site repair support.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
These are the most significant job duties performed. The size, scope and complexity of assigned duties and responsibilities are dependent on the level and experience of the incumbent. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each assigned essential duty satisfactorily. Other responsibilities or special projects not specifically listed below may also be assigned.
Installs basic mechanical commercial food equipment and assists in more advanced installs as needed.
Maintain, diagnose, and repair basic mechanical commercial food equipment for customers on contract and/or on time and material (i.e., T&M) basis.
Completes and documents preventative maintenance on basic mechanical commercial food equipment.
Implements and supports standard operating procedures outlined in Hobart Service safety manuals and programs.
Supports branch and organization financial objectives by providing a quality customer experience.
Maintains current organization, industry, and equipment knowledge.
Responsible for assigned company assets including vehicle, tools, and inventory.
Follows the company's safe driving and other applicable policies.
Supervisory Responsibilities
This position has no direct or indirect supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required to perform this job successfully. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Required Education and Work Experience
High school diploma or GED and,
0-2 years of electrical/mechanical experience
Desired Education/Experience
Associates Degree or Vocational Certificate is preferred.
Mechanical or electrical experience is preferred.
Experience installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing commercial cooking and/or refrigeration equipment is preferred.
Certificates and Licenses
Position/Location dependent.
Job Specific Knowledge
To perform this job successfully, the individual needs to demonstrate knowledge of these areas as they relate to the primary functions of the job.
Mechanical Aptitude – demonstrates mechanical aptitude to operate and troubleshoot equipment. Skilled in use of various tools and equipment (e.g. basic hand tools, reading and following service manuals, gauges, meters, etc.)
Customer Service - highly professional demeanor with excellent telephone skills and etiquette. Utilizes various interpersonal styles and communication methods to positively assist and influence customers.
Problem Solving - fundamental role in finding ways to address all types of problems by having a good approach to a problem without being ineffective, favoring or causing painful consequences.
Safety at Work - learns to keep the organization safe from different risks by developing a high sense of alertness that detects danger from afar and stops it before it causes risk, danger or injury to themselves, or others.
COMPETENCIES
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies.
Technical and Analytical Skills
Ability to read and interpret standard service manuals, mechanical diagrams, sustains understanding of parts stocking and identification methods, practices, and procedures.
Understanding of basic math (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, calculations of percentages, measurement conversions)
Ensure they are following workflow processes (e.g., Inspection accuracy)
Understanding and promoting sales/lead opportunities to assist in creating customer-focused strategies for fostering business relationships (e.g., equipment leads, contract leads, water treatment order leads).
Basic knowledge of / working knowledge of Windows applications and Microsoft Office programs such as Word and Excel.

Applies feedback to improve performance.

title: Strategic Buyer
description:
Job Description:
Brooks Instrument, an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a Strategic Buyer position that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia) but report to the Global Industrial Supply Chain Manager in Székesfehérvár, Hungary. The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, Hungary, Malaysia and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
Identify, implement and manage supplier relationships to support operational requirements at the lowest total cost consistent with Company policies, procedures, as well as Company Values and quality standards.  Responsible for researching and identifying suppliers for materials across the Brooks network, working closely with cross functional teams to develop supply sourcing strategies that reduce cost, ensure continuity of supply, and meet Brooks quality requirements.  Responsible for leading Brooks’ supplier management efforts for key suppliers, and for ensuring compliance with Brooks’ purchasing policies and procedures, ethical practices, and adherence to relevant laws and regulations.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
*Marginal position functions that are not included among the essential duties and responsibilities in this position description are also requirements of this position.
Develop long-range sourcing plans for key commodities using appropriate thinking, behavior and practices.
Select suppliers, conduct supplier negotiations, establish and monitor supply agreements.
Effectively apply ITW business process tools such as 80/20, USa, and MRD to all aspects of Brooks supply chain
Develop and implement effective cost management programs to deliver optimized Total Cost of Ownership and continuous cost improvement
Optimize value delivery from suppliers.
Measure and review supplier performance and lead supplier continuous improvement programs.
Execute plans to assure continuous supply of quality goods and services
Execute plans to combat market changes and challenges
Support the Quality and Operational teams to ensure that our suppliers meet our quality requirements and applicable technical
Support Supplier problem resolution as appropriate for assigned portfolio.
Manage and monitor material changes for compliance to quality and technical standards.

description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful?
Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader
in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da
Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of
patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery
smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater
precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging,
but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a
life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future
of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
The Chief of Staff, Corporate Strategy will report to the Head of Corporate Strategy. This role serves as her key operating and coordination partner, ensuring that Intuitive’s enterprise-wide strategic agenda runs smoothly day to day — from the cadence of key strategy meetings to the follow-through on priority workstreams across the organization. This is a unique opportunity to sit at the center of Intuitive’s corporate strategy function, with visibility into the company’s most important strategic decisions.
The Chief of Staff will own the operating rhythm of the Corporate Strategy function, including planning and facilitating key strategy meetings and related forums, tracking progress and decisions across the enterprise-wide strategic workstream portfolio, and ensuring information flows efficiently between the Head of Corporate Strategy, DRIs, executive sponsors, and the CEO. Success requires exceptional organizational rigor, sound judgment, the ability to synthesize complex information quickly, and the trust and discretion to operate close to the CEO and senior leadership.
Key Responsibilities
Own the operating rhythm of the Corporate Strategy function, including planning, agenda-setting, and follow-through for key strategy meetings and other recurring strategic forums.
Partner with the Head of Corporate Strategy to prioritize her time and attention across the enterprise-wide strategic workstream portfolio, surfacing the issues and decisions that most need her focus.
Track progress, decisions, and action items across enterprise-wide strategic workstreams, holding DRIs and executive sponsors accountable for timely follow-through.
Prepare, review, and quality-control materials, briefings, and presentations for key strategy meetings, senior leadership, and other executive forums.
Serve as a trusted thought partner and sounding board to the Head of Corporate Strategy on emerging issues, priorities, and organizational dynamics.
Manage the flow of information between the Corporate Strategy function and leaders across the organization, ensuring the right people have the right information at the right time.
Identify and help remove roadblocks to progress on strategic initiatives, escalating issues appropriately and driving resolution.
Lead special projects and analyses on behalf of the Head of Corporate Strategy as enterprise priorities evolve.
Support team operations for the Corporate Strategy function, including planning, resource allocation, and talent processes as needed.
Represent the Head of Corporate Strategy in select meetings and forums, ensuring continuity and consistent messaging across the organization.
Required Skills and Experience
Bachelor's degree required; MBA or other advanced degree preferred.
12+ years of progressive professional experience, ideally spanning strategy consulting, corporate strategy, executive or chief-of-staff roles, or an equivalent analytical/operational role, preferably within medical device or broader healthcare industries.
Demonstrated experience operating in a chief-of-staff, executive-office, or similar role supporting senior leaders, ideally within a large, matrixed organization.
Exceptional organizational and program-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and competing priorities.
Strong executive communication skills, including experience preparing materials for and presenting to senior executives and boards.
Sound judgment and discretion in handling highly sensitive and confidential information.
Proven ability to build trust and influence across a large, matrixed organization without relying on formal authority.
Strong written synthesis skills; able to distill complex, ambiguous information into clear, decision-ready recommendations.
High degree of professional judgment, integrity, and ownership.

description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Job Description
The Human Factors Manager works closely with fellow Human Factors managers and engineers and collaborates with other cross-functional managers of clinical engineering, system and software engineering, product managers, and program managers among other important functional teams in the development of novel technologies and devices.
The Human Factors Manager's primary role is to support, inform and guide development of Human Factors team members and represent the Human Factors function within and across business units, ensuring the successful execution of Human Factors Usability Engineering Initiatives, process activities and deliverables, while keeping a patient-first mindset, acting as an advocate for the clinical caregiver end-users regarding safety and usability, and as representative for medical device regulatory compliance.
As a member of new product-development project teams, the Human Factors Manager leads as a key stakeholder within a creative and structured process to help their direct HF team plan, communicate and advocate the value of Human factors function, and execute the appropriate scale of usability engineering activities prior to launch, within a regulated design controls environment.
Establish and support project-based strategy for usability research, consistent with research strategy and initiatives across the Human Factors group.
Forecast planning and budgeting for needed usability research and testing efforts, including estimates for needed resources and equipment.
Mentor, support and guide HF team members in the translation of design insights into actionable usability considerations and requirements and proactively collaborate with design engineering partners to ensure best in class usability.
Support the execution of, and report to leadership on, usability research and evaluations at various stages of product development.
The Human Factors Manger will balance testing efforts across multiple projects from early prototypes to formal External Standards-mandated validation testing in US and OUS market environments.
Advocate strongly and consistently for the clinical caregiver experience for safety and usability, with understanding of the nuance and balance of user/customer needs and business needs.
Interface and associate with end-user customers in multiple international markets to gather design insights in a highly professional manner, during complex workflow-oriented usability formative study and user research activities.
Write and revise highly accurate, clear, and concise usability engineering documents in a timely manner for multiple projects.
Synthesize complex information into internal communications and presentations for product teams and broader organization leadership audiences.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies, including supporting the response to questions for additional justification and rationale
What You'll Bring
Minimum Education: BS in Human Factors Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Cognitive Psychology, Computer Science with human-computer interface (HCI) emphasis, Human Centered Design, or related field. MS strongly preferred.
Minimum of 5 years of related team management experience with a Bachelor’s degree (in engineering); or 3 years and a Master’s degree; or a relevant PhD with 4 years experience; or equivalent experience with human factors/biomedical devices.
Experience in medical device product development within a design controls process or healthcare setting (or similar highly regulated industry) is required.
Demonstrated experience in HF (UX) and User Research project management.
Demonstrated experience of successful execution or direct support of global regulatory submissions.
Keep abreast of regulations and best practices for medical device
human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills working within a highly statured communication environment using multiple communication channels (email, text, video conference, instant messaging platforms).
Experience working with Digital project collaboration tools is appreciated. (e.g. Mural, Smartsheets, etc).
Demonstrated ability to advocate and effectively champion user-centered design and usability engineering principles to product research, development, and design in a fast-paced product development environment.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with and across various functional leadership and levels of management within the organization, including other engineering groups, marketing, clinical engineering, and regulatory to solve complex usability issues involving detailed risk analysis.
Ability to travel internationally as well as domestically (up to 20%; 25-30%)

Experience with rapid prototyping methods for instruments, components, and fixtures, including 3D printing and machining of plastics and metals

Experience working with suppliers
Ability to work independently under limited supervision while knowing when to escalate
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Effective written and verbal communication

Experience with flexible electromechanical device development is a strong plus

The Senior Human Factors Engineer works closely with designers, clinical engineers, and technical product managers to inform and guide the development of new products and ensure that those products are safe and easy to use. Roles & Responsibilities:
Collect and synthesize detailed information on how users interact with Intuitive products through various techniques including interviews, simulations, direct observations, task analyses, and persona development.

Design, execute, and report on usability (human factors) tests at various stages of product development from early prototypes all the way through formal FDA-mandated validation testing.
Write and execute usability test protocols. Analyze test data and write test reports.
Develop validation strategies for projects involving updates to existing products.
Lead the efforts required to create and update usability risk analyses for Intuitive products
Maintain traces between use risks, mitigations, and validation test cases.
Reinforce a human centered design approach across the organization.
Represent the Human Factors function on core teams for large projects.
Coordinate human factors efforts across projects involving several sub-systems.
Manage usability engineering activities within development projects and provide schedules and status to technical product managers and engineering project managers.
Mentor junior human factors engineers (e.g. interns) and others in organization in usability engineering methods and best practices, as well as Intuitive product development processes.
Prepare and review documentation for submission to regulatory agencies and notified bodies.
Answer questions and provide additional justification and rationale to any questions received.
Keep abreast of regulations and best practices for medical device human factors (e.g. IEC 62366, AAMI HE75, FDA Applying Human Factors and Usability Engineering to Medical Devices) and advise management regarding potential improvements to internal processes and regulatory issues related to usability engineering.

Minimum BS in Human Factors Engineering, Cognitive Psychology, Computer Science with human-computer interface (HCI) emphasis, Human Centered Design, or related field. MS strongly preferred.
Minimum 8+ years relevant Human Factors/Usability Engineering experience in hardware product development industry
Experience in medical device, or similar regulated industry, a significant plus
Ability to lead usability engineering activities (i.e. establishing usability requirements; creating usability risk analyses, test protocols, and test reports) for a complex, software-controlled electro-mechanical medical device
Ability to interface with customers in a highly professional manner
Ability to analyze and synthesize large quantities of information into usable communications
Superior ability to write accurate, clear, and concise protocols, reports, operating procedures, etc. in a timely manner
Excellent verbal communication and presentation skills
Ability to work with and across various groups and levels of management within the organization, including other engineering groups, marketing, clinical engineering, and regulatory. Excellent collaboration skills.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills and familiarity with technical writing

The Production Supervisor is a member of the plant leadership team and is responsible for day-to-day manufacturing operations within an assigned area and shift under the direction of the Business Unit Manager. This role provides leadership to deliver business results and operational improvements while achieving productivity, efficiency, customer service, cost, quality, safety, and employee engagement objectives through individual and team contributions.
Key Responsibilities
Manage day-to-day manufacturing operations for the assigned area and shift to meet productivity, efficiency, customer service, cost, quality, safety, and employee engagement objectives.
Provide direction, leadership, development, and support to direct reports through empowerment, teamwork, on-the-job assignments, and continuous improvement projects and initiatives.
Develop, implement, and promote safety programs and safe work practices through participation in plant safety teams, programs, and initiatives.
Promote sound employee and labor relations within the department by developing and maintaining an effective organization with qualified personnel.
Develop, promote, and support continuous improvement efforts and cross-functional initiatives that deliver business results and operational improvements.

Shift execution: Translate production priorities into daily assignments, communicate expectations, and coordinate staffing, materials, and equipment readiness to support the production schedule.
Operational results: Monitor production output, downtime, waste, yield, and labor utilization. Identify deviations, communicate barriers, and coordinate corrective actions with appropriate support teams.
Safety leadership: Reinforce established safety procedures, personal protective equipment requirements, housekeeping standards, and hazard reporting. Escalate unsafe conditions and support incident reviews and corrective-action follow-through.
Food safety and quality: Partner with Quality and Food Safety personnel to reinforce good manufacturing practices, sanitation requirements, product specifications, and required production checks. Escalate deviations and follow established product hold and disposition procedures.
Cross-functional coordination: Work with Maintenance, Sanitation, Planning, and Warehouse teams to address equipment concerns, changeovers, material availability, and other issues affecting safe and reliable production.

Employee communication: Conduct shift meetings, communicate operational updates, recognize team contributions, and promptly elevate employee concerns to the appropriate leader or Human Resources.
Labor relations: Partner with Human Resources and plant leadership to apply established policies and applicable collective bargaining agreement provisions consistently when coordinating assignments, staffing, and employee matters.
Continuous improvement: Use production data and team input to identify recurring losses, support root-cause analysis, implement approved improvements, and confirm that corrective actions are sustained.
Documentation and handoffs: Maintain accurate production records and shift reports. Communicate equipment status, unresolved issues, quality concerns, staffing needs, and follow-up actions to the incoming shift.

BA/BS Degree in Business, Food Science, Engineering or related field is preferred

Strong communication and leadership skills
Strong analytical/critical thinking
Strong accountability, consistency and follow-through skills
Ability to work effectively with a wide array of plant personnel ranging from hourly employees to senior management

Provide first-level, day-to-day administrative and technical supervision for a staff of professional engineers and technicians within an engineering department unit to accomplish specific engineering projects. Review technical feasibility of proposed solutions to engineering problems. Specialize in areas of competence (electrical, mechanical, etc.) depending on the function, according to the type of product or process. Responsible for the results of the unit's efforts and for the effectiveness of their overall integration within other units. Direct work assignments, scheduling, and reviews of work in progress. Typically lead a staff of five to ten professionals.
Job Description
Job Purpose
The Refrigeration, HVAC, Plant System Design Engineer is a subject matter expert that will lead their discipline as part of the Design and Technical Capabilities team to define standards, consistent processes, and formulate projects that can be used and issued to suppliers for initial budget and final pricing and order placement. The design engineer is responsible for the design, operation, maintenance, and optimization of ammonia-based refrigeration systems used in industries such as food processing, cold storage, and manufacturing. This role requires a strong engineering background, deep technical knowledge of ammonia systems, and strict adherence to safety and regulatory standards. The specialized professional focus will be on ammonia/refrigeration but their responsible will includes oversight of design, engineering, safety and quality support in the following utility equipment systems: Clean steam, RO systems, HVAC systems, plant steam systems, process chillers, compressed/process air, nitrogen, ammonia chillers, refrigeration process, and cooling towers. This individual will work closely with a cross-functional team to meet the needs of the groups they support. This position supports the team on completing capital engineering feasibility studies, develop initial and detailed equipment designs, and creating engineering standards that complement the equipment design and can be utilized for project feasibility and execution phases of projects to improve speed of execution. This individual will require both the project management and technical knowledge to develop the scope for complex utilities projects. While this role will be focused on refrigeration/ammonia expertise, team members are expected to have general knowledge of infrastructure, utilities, wastewater treatment and food and beverages process technologies.

Review PSM audits and provide solutions and alternative options. · Create standard engineering project designs and Capex estimates for major capital initiatives working together with supply development, project leads and their teams. · Provide engineering support to address operational / compliance issues and to ensure equipment is maintained at a level required to provide high reliability maximizing useful life · Provide technical expertise and industry best practices · Lead engineering efforts to resolve equipment and operational problems and ensure problem solving techniques are appropriately utilized · Participate & lead cross functional reviews to define and agree standard process flows ensure all major Capital projects (>$1MM) within the Zone are designed to maintain business continuity, maximize operating income and factory efficiency, including the formulation of: standard designs, cost estimation and challenging timelines together with BU Engineering, ORM, R&D and FS&Q. · Develop equipment standards and designs to enable Procurement to obtain standard pricing structures for particular/preferred suppliers. · Establish benchmarking of common equipment or processes and Capital projects across the Zone to understand key advantages of each the various installed lines and standardize where these bring competitive advantage. · Identify and evaluate Best Available Technologies and engineering practices for their discipline, sharing them across the zone, and globally where appropriate. guide the business towards the best ROI capital investments. · Develop project design, detailed scopes of work, cost estimates, timelines and bid documentation for capital projects that are identified as high potential for investment. · Work with third party engineering firms to develop for-bid and for-construction drawings. · Act as a resident expert within ammonia/refrigeration field of stakeholders (OEM’s, Contractors, local utility) to ensure that they are aligned with the Kraft Heinz direction and deliver maximum value for our investments. · Scout, evaluate, and qualify potential practices. Role Overview
The Head of Occupational Health provides global medical leadership to protect the health, wellbeing, and work capability of our global workforce.
In this role, you will establish global occupational health standards, design the multi-year strategy, and ensure robust clinical governance and regulatory compliance. Working in close partnership with Health & Safety, People & Organization (P&O), Operations, and Benefits, you will drive continuous improvement in workforce health protection, ensuring a safe, inclusive, and highly resilient working environment.
Key Accountabilities
1. Global Strategy & Medical Leadership
Set the Vision: Develop and execute the global occupational health strategy, establishing clear priorities, standards, and a multi-year roadmap.
Alignment: Ensure the strategy aligns seamlessly with broader business needs, workforce health risks, and organizational objectives.
2. Risk Prevention & Management
Risk Assessment: Provide deep medical expertise to identify, assess, and prevent work-related health risks, including occupational exposures, physical hazards, and psychosocial risks.
Collaboration: Partner with Health & Safety and Operations to design and implement highly effective, preventative controls.
3. Clinical Governance & Regulatory Compliance
Standard Setting: Establish global clinical standards, protocols, and assurance frameworks to ensure safe, evidence-based occupational health practices.
Compliance: Oversee medical surveillance programs and ensure strict adherence to local legislations, professional practices, and confidentiality standards globally.
4. Workforce Health & Fitness for Work
Employee Support: Provide medical leadership for fitness-for-work assessments, rehabilitation, reasonable workplace adjustments, and return-to-work processes.
Inclusion: Champion workplace adjustments that support diverse physical capabilities, inclusion, and sustained employee capability.
5. Health Intelligence & Performance Management
Data-Driven Insights: Define key occupational health metrics, analyze workforce health trends, and deliver actionable insights to senior leadership.
Continuous Improvement: Use health intelligence to drive evidence-based interventions and track measurable health outcomes.
6. Service Delivery & Strategic Partnership
Operating Model: Define the global operating model and set standards for external occupational health service providers.
Team Capability: Build the capability and competency of regional and local health teams.
Cross-Functional Synergy: Partner with Benefits, Security, P&O, and Business Leaders on wellness promotion, emergency medical preparedness, and crisis management.
Experience & Capabilities
Required Qualifications
Credentials: Fully qualified Occupational Health Physician with recognized advanced qualifications/board certification in Occupational Medicine.
Experience: 15+ years of progressive, hands-on leadership experience in Occupational Medicine within a large multinational organization. This includes leading strategy across multiple geographies with differing legal frameworks.
Strategic Leadership: Proven track record of designing and implementing global occupational health strategies, with deep expertise in health risk management and clinical governance.
Business Partnering & Influence: Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead organizational change in highly complex, matrixed environments.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience operating within highly complex operational, manufacturing, or supply-chain environments.
Proven experience leading enterprise-level wellness, mental health, or occupational health initiatives.
Recognized external thought leadership in Occupational Health or Public Health forums.
Leadership Capabilities

Strategic Mindset & Global Perspective – Able to look ahead to future possibilities and translate them into breakthrough strategies with a global lens.
Drives Vision & Purpose – Painting a compelling picture of the health vision that motivates others to action.
Balances Stakeholders & Organizational Savvy – Navigating complex matrix dynamics and balancing the needs of multiple stakeholder groups.
Plans, Aligns, & Ensures Accountability – Planning work to meet commitments, aligning regional teams, and holding self and others accountable.

Def i ning Success in the Role

Measurable Improvements in workforce health protection and the reduction of work-related illnesses.

title: Learning Business Partner
description:
Job Description:
The Learning Business Partner acts as a strategic co-pilot and advisor to senior business leaders, driving organizational performance by translating complex business strategies into sustainable capability architectures.
This role owns the end-to-end learning value chain—from strategic business relationship management and performance consulting to learning needs analysis, high-level learning solution design, and evaluation. This role creates high-impact capability strategies and designs holistic learning experiences that seamlessly integrate into the daily flow of work, directly enabling business growth and Associate skill building
Key Responsibilities
1. Performance Consulting & Stakeholder Relationship Management (Consulting & Influence)
·         Strategic Business Partnership: Act as the primary interface and trusted advisor to stakeholders. Proactively manage senior stakeholder relationships, establishing credibility to influence decision-making and champion the enterprise learning agenda.
·         Performance Diagnostics: Use advanced performance consulting methodologies to diagnose organizational performance challenges. Conduct root-cause analyses to distinguish between training opportunities and other organizational, process, or talent-related interventions.
·         Demand & Portfolio Management: Effectively manage and prioritize the pipeline of learning requests. Act as a strategic gateway, aligning proposed learning solutions with key business priorities and long-term talent strategies.
2. Learning Needs Analysis & Capability Architecture (Skills & Learning Strategy)
·         Diagnostic Skills Assessment: Apply quantitative and qualitative research methodologies (surveys, data benchmarks, focus groups, interviews) to map existing skills inventories, isolate skill gaps, and define the critical capabilities required for future-readiness.
·         Capability & Skills Architecture: Design and maintain agile skills matrices and capability frameworks aligned with business strategies. Define current versus ideal performance states and design scalable learning pathways to close the gap.
·         Enterprise Synergy: Collaborate across functional domains to identify horizontal capability trends, scaling successful learning models and preventing fragmented, redundant initiatives.
3. Holistic Learning Solution Design (Design & Orchestration)
·         High-Level Solution Design: Map human-centered learner journeys and establish robust instructional design frameworks. Architect multi-faceted learning ecosystems that integrate formal, social, and experiential (70/20/10) learning components.
·         Modality & Technology Selection: Evaluate and select optimal delivery formats (digital self-paced, synchronous virtual, classroom, social learning networks, or workflow-embedded tools) that maximize engagement and drive behavioral change.
·         ID Partnering & Quality Assurance: Define and document high-level design specifications and standards for external and internal Instructional Design (ID) partners. Collaborate closely during the build phase, maintaining accountability for the overall design integrity, context alignment, and deployment success.
4. Data Literacy, Measurement, and Impact (Analytics & Valuation)
·         Success Metrics Definition: Define key performance indicators (KPIs) and business impact metrics at the outset of every initiative in collaboration with business sponsors.
·         Measurement & Evaluation: Apply robust evaluation frameworks (e.g., LTEM, Kirkpatrick) to monitor learner engagement, behavior change, and business ROI.
·         Insights-Driven Optimization: Analyze data to derive insights, communicate the strategic value of learning to executive leadership, and continuously optimize the portfolio.
Context and Scope
The Learning Business Partner operates in a fast-paced, highly matrixed, global environment. The role holder must successfully navigate complex stakeholder landscapes across global segments, cultures, and time zones.
The role operates at the critical intersection of business leaders and centralized learning execution teams. Rather than producing raw training content, the Learning Business Partner owns the "What" and "Why “defining the strategic learning agenda and designing the learner experience—while steering the "How" in partnership with Instructional Designers and vendors. The position requires a high degree of autonomy, executive presence, and the ability to influence without authority.
Job Specifications / Qualifications
Education & Professional Qualifications
·         Minimum Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in Learning & Development
·         Global Readiness: Demonstrated capability to operate effectively across diverse geographical regions and cultures. Regular availability to support US/European time zones is required.
·         Travel: Ability to travel up to 10% of the time for key stakeholder alignment meetings and learning forums.
Key Knowledge & Experience
·         Consulting & Influence: Masterful ability to conduct diagnostics, build trusted-advisor relationships, manage expectation mismatches, and influence VP/Director-level stakeholders.
·         Business & Functional Acumen: Deep understanding of corporate structures and business value chains (Sales, Supply, R&D, Finance, P&O, etc.) with the ability to speak the language of business leaders.
·         Digital Fluency & AI Capability: Savviness in utilizing modern learning technology stacks (LMS, LXP, social learning environments) and emerging AI capabilities for automated curation, skill taxonomy tagging, and personalized learning journeys.
·         Data Literacy: Proven experience defining data collection methodologies, reading dashboards, interpreting learner analytics, and synthesizing data points into executive-level narratives.
·         Adult Learning Strategy: Expert-level knowledge of adult learning theories, cognitive design principles, behavioral economics/change management, and 70/20/10 operationalization.
Competency Profile
Key Mars Leadership Competencies
·         Strategic Mindset: Sees ahead to future possibilities and translates them into breakthrough strategies.
·         Balances Stakeholders: Anticipates and balances the needs of multiple stakeholders across a matrix.
·         Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
·         Manages Ambiguity: Operates effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is unclear.
·         Nimble Learning: Learns quickly when facing new situations, experimenting to find solutions.
·         Plans & Aligns: Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
Key Functional Competencies & Technical Skills
1.       Performance Consulting & Business Advising (Advanced): High-impact capability to discover actual business drivers, separate skill deficiencies from structural or operational issues, and co-create performance-improving interventions.
2.       Capability & Skills Architecture (Advanced): Ability to translate business strategies into structured, agile skills-based taxonomies, job architectures, and progressive learning paths.
3.       End-to-End Learning Strategy & Experience Design (Advanced): Mastery over designing comprehensive user journeys and program architectures using modern modalities that drive business change.
4.       Data-Driven Measurement & Impact Assessment (Advanced): Proven competence in defining and measuring learning metrics tied directly to business results, using data to inform program iterations.
5.       Digital Fluency & Digital Curation (Advanced): Strategic capability to leverage artificial intelligence, collaborative platforms, and modern LXPs to scale social and self-directed learning experiences.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

OpenAI is seeking a hands-on Art Director to partner with the Research team on creative concepts, visual direction, and design. You’ll help define how research stories look and feel, developing ideas and carrying them into compelling visual work. Working directly with researchers, you’ll keep scientific accuracy and clarity central to the creative approach, while finding distinctive ways to capture people’s attention and imagination.

You’ll collaborate with filmmakers, designers, and marketing and creative partners across web, social, film, editorial, and experiences. Your work may range from developing a visual concept and art directing collaborators to designing assets yourself. You’ll create treatments, references, and explorations that establish a clear direction, then help carry that direction through production and final delivery.

This role suits a versatile art director with strong hands-on design craft, a distinct creative point of view, and an interest in AI research. You can move between the overall visual idea and the details of execution, build cohesive visual systems, and give collaborators clear, constructive feedback. You should be comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting your approach to an evolving research agenda.

 - Partner with researchers and creative teams to understand priorities, develop original concepts, and define the visual direction for research stories, announcements, and demos; communicate ideas through treatments, mood boards, references, and design explorations

title: Counsel, AI Safety & Cyber Incident Response
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Legal team helps address the cutting-edge legal questions that arise from developing and deploying advanced AI. The Security and Public Sector Legal team helps protect OpenAI’s technology, systems, data, and people and supports the safe and responsible use of our tools. We work closely with technical and operational teams to provide practical advice on novel, consequential, and fast-moving issues.



About the Role

We are seeking a counsel to help lead legal responses to cybersecurity and AI safety incidents. This is an opportunity to bring deep incident response expertise to some of the hardest questions in AI, and help build the legal frameworks and practices for answering them.



You will advise on complex cybersecurity incidents, from discovery through to resolution, and also help develop our response to incidents involving the safety of our models and tools. AI safety incident response is a new and rapidly evolving legal practice area. Your work will help define how frontier AI companies investigate and respond to safety events such as unexpected model behavior, degradation of safeguards, harmful uses of our services, and potential harm to third parties—often where established legal standards do not yet exist. Working directly with Security, Safety, Product, Engineering, and colleagues across Legal, you will advise on consequential decisions where established approaches may offer little guidance.



We are looking for a practical, dynamic lawyer who can turn incomplete information into clear recommendations, exercise sound judgment on novel questions, and follow matters through to resolution. You will help establish the facts, assess risks, and guide investigations, communications, remediation, and reporting. You will also turn lessons from individual incidents into durable response processes, helping further develop a legal function that evolves alongside the technology.



This role is based in Washington, D.C. or San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In this role, you will be:

 - Serving as legal lead on assigned cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, coordinating fact development, legal analysis and advising, cross-functional escalation, and follow-through with the response team.

 - Working with investigators to understand incident scope, attack paths, root cause, and affected systems and data, and potential third-party impacts, while helping teams distinguish established facts from gaps in the evidence.

 - Managing outside counsel and third party service provider engagements necessary to incident response.

 - Serving as key Legal point of contact for cross-functional teams.

 - Partnering with Privacy, Product, Regulatory, and other counsel to assess notification and reporting obligations, advise on timely customer and user communications, and coordinate third-party outreach and incident-related information sharing with industry peers and government partners.

 - Preparing concise incident updates and decision materials that distinguish established facts, uncertainties, options, and recommended next steps.

 - Developing severity-based escalation criteria, response playbooks, exercises, and clear decision and handoff processes for cybersecurity and AI safety incidents, adapting established practices to emerging model risks.

 - Supporting post-incident reviews, tracking agreed corrective actions, and turning lessons into practical improvements to safeguards and response processes.

 - A JD and a license or qualification to practice law in your jurisdiction.

 - 5+ years of relevant experience.

 - The ability to translate technical findings into practical legal advice, with a working understanding of technical information.

 - Sound judgment under time pressure, clear communication of uncertainty, and an understanding of when to act, seek specialist advice, or escalate.

 - Clear, concise writing and the ability to keep cross-functional teams aligned through changing facts and competing priorities.

 - Ownership of details and follow-through, paired with collaborative work with colleagues who bring different expertise.

About the Team

API Multicloud partners with cloud service providers (CSPs) to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and APIs into the cloud environments where developers and enterprises already build. We own the API end to end across CSP platforms, from API integration and request routing through inference execution, capacity management, and day-to-day operations. Our mission is to make these capabilities available broadly and safely while preserving the reliability and developer experience customers expect from OpenAI.

Delivering that experience requires work across the stack: adapting API services and cloud-native integrations, bringing up model-serving environments, validating new releases, and operating the systems that connect customer requests to available capacity. We work directly with CSP engineering teams and partner closely with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems teams. Together, we turn new model capabilities and partner requirements into dependable production services, with attention to performance, operational readiness, and efficient use of compute.

Our work contributes to OpenAI’s AWS partnership https://openai.com/index/openai-on-aws/, including the launch of Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/openai-daybreak-red-and-blue-on-amazon-bedrock/ — and OpenAI’s newly announced Google Cloud partnership https://openai.com/index/openai-models-google-cloud/ will bring our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. title: ML Silicon Performance Lead
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM:

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

We’re looking for an ML Silicon Performance Lead to drive hardware/software co-design for our silicon architecture. You will work across models, kernels, compilers, and silicon to shape how ML workloads map to hardware—and how the hardware should evolve to support them. Your work will connect model and workload requirements with compute, memory, and specialized acceleration capabilities to maximize performance, efficiency, and scalability across current and future generations of AI silicon.

You’ll partner closely with ML research, compiler, and silicon architecture teams to jointly develop software approaches and hardware capabilities. From kernel mapping and quantization to new data structures and specialized IP, you’ll evaluate hardware and software tradeoffs to improve performance, efficiency, and utilization across large-scale AI workloads. Through performance modeling, simulation, and hands-on optimization, you’ll guide architectural decisions and validate improvements on representative workloads.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Drive hardware/software co-design across ML research, compiler, and silicon teams, jointly shaping kernel implementations and hardware capabilities to meet workload performance and efficiency goals.

 - Partner with ML research to translate model and workload needs into kernel performance targets and compute, memory capacity, and bandwidth requirements, feeding hardware constraints and opportunities back into model and algorithm choices.

 - Map and optimize ML kernels for architecture, using insights from data movement, memory hierarchy, and execution efficiency to guide both software improvements and hardware design.

 - Co-design support for new data structures and quantization formats across kernels, compilers, and silicon, balancing model quality, numerical behavior, performance, power, and implementation cost.

 - Define and help develop specialized acceleration IP, working with compiler and silicon partners to determine the right division of functionality across software, instructions, and dedicated hardware.

 - Drive ML performance modeling and simulation with the compiler team to compare hardware/software design options, expose bottlenecks, and quantify end-to-end benefits on representative workloads.

 - Partner with the Silicon Architecture lead and silicon team to specify and validate new IP, using kernel and simulation results to refine requirements and prioritize architectural improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have deep experience with ML accelerator architecture and how compute resources, memory systems, and data movement shape workload performance.

 - Can translate model-level behavior into concrete kernel requirements and hardware design decisions.

 - Have built or used accelerator performance models and simulators, and know how to validate their assumptions and interpret their limitations.

 - Have hands-on experience optimizing ML kernels, including identifying bottlenecks and improving utilization, locality, and execution efficiency.

 - Understand quantization and numerical formats, including their implications for model quality, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and hardware support.

 - Have experience with hardware/software co-design and can reason about whether a capability belongs in a kernel, compiler, instruction set, or dedicated hardware.

 - Work effectively across research, compiler, and silicon teams, bringing clarity to ambiguous requirements and building alignment through technical evidence.

title: Staff Backend Engineer, Financial Engineering
description:
About the Team

Financial Engineering (FinEng) builds the financial systems behind ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI’s API platform. These products serve people, developers, and businesses around the world. We make them easy to buy, use, and pay for. Our systems support everything from individual subscriptions to usage-based billing and complex enterprise agreements.

We also build the foundations for how products are packaged, accessed, and used: product catalogs, SKUs and bundles, workspaces, entitlements, and usage metering. These systems connect what customers purchase to the capabilities they can access and the usage they can manage.

That reach creates challenging engineering problems. We build services and data pipelines that handle large volumes of usage and transactions, keep payments, product access, and financial records consistent across systems, and adapt as products and pricing change. The same foundations must support a simple checkout and the detailed spending controls a large business needs.

Your work will help teams launch new products faster and give customers confidence in what they are paying for. The work spans customer experiences, backend services, and data systems, with opportunities to influence technical design and see your work through to production.

We’re hiring Staff+ engineers with strong backend experience. Experience in payments, billing, or financial systems is a strong plus, but not required.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and build systems for purchasing, payments, subscriptions, and billing across OpenAI products and global markets.

 - Build product catalogs, SKUs, and bundles that let product teams launch new offerings and evolve how products are packaged.

 - Develop workspace and entitlement systems that connect purchases and subscriptions to product access for individuals and teams.

 - Keep charges and product access correct when requests are retried, updates arrive late, or another service fails.

 - Build metering systems, data pipelines, and APIs that turn large volumes of usage into accurate bills, timely spending information, and records that are easy to trace and verify.

 - Create reusable building blocks that let product teams launch new offerings, pricing, and payment options without rebuilding the foundations each time.

 - Make complex financial workflows simple for customers and internal teams, using customer feedback and experiments to improve the experience.

 - Scale and evolve live systems while protecting customer access, financial accuracy, performance, and security.

 - Own problems from early design through launch and operation, working with product, design, finance, and other engineering teams to make and test important technical decisions.

Nice to Have

 - Experience with payments, subscriptions, pricing, billing, or other systems that manage customer purchases and revenue.

 - Experience with product catalogs, packaging and bundles, workspace management, entitlements, or usage metering.

 - Experience building financial or transaction systems at scale, checking that records match across systems, or supporting compliance and audits.

title: Sr. Manager, Procure to Pay
description:

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
You will own the end-to-end Procure-to-Pay (P2P) function, spanning Procurement Operations, Accounts Payable, supplier onboarding, and payments. You will set the governance model and service standards, partner with executive stakeholders, and build a team that delivers consistently.
In this role, you will:
Own end-to-end P2P performance, from requisition and PO through receipt, invoice, approval, payment, and accrual, and align every tower (Procurement, AP, Supplier Management, Payments, Close) to one operating model
Establish and enforce operational governance: policies, controls, SLAs/KPIs, approval matrices, and audit readiness (SOX), with regular performance reviews
Ensure accurate, timely processing of requisitions, POs, and invoices, and the completeness of accruals and liability reconciliations for the financial close
Design supplier onboarding and master-data standards, with attention to risk, compliance, and payment integrity
Own payment-run integrity, including approval controls, banking batch oversight, and fraud and duplicate-payment prevention
Resolve escalated payment and process issues, and use root-cause research to prevent repeat issues
Partner with suppliers, Procurement, Finance, Legal, IT, and business stakeholders to define and deliver the automation and transformation roadmap
Report on P2P performance using defined KPIs (touchless invoice rate, on-time payment, cycle time, exception rate, DPO) and optimize working capital through payment terms and early-pay discounts
Oversee supplier risk, contract and PO compliance, and spend visibility across the vendor base
Manage change by rolling out policy, process, and system updates with clear stakeholder communication and adoption tracking
Elevate customer satisfaction across internal stakeholders and suppliers by owning the service experience, measuring CSAT/NPS, and acting on feedback
Deliver quarterly business reviews with senior and executive stakeholders, presenting performance, risks, and the improvement roadmap
Hire, develop, and coach a high-performing team, and hold every team member to a consistent standard through documented processes, training, performance calibration, and clear accountability
Build the training, onboarding, and succession plans that keep team capability uniform across locations
Model and embed Samsara’s values as the team scales globally
Minimum requirements for the role:
10+ years in procure-to-pay, AP, or procurement operations, including 5+ years managing teams and managers
Demonstrated end-to-end P2P expertise across multiple towers, with the ability to align cross-functional dependencies
Track record of running operational governance: SLAs, KPIs, internal controls, and audit/SOX compliance
Experience owning a team budget, managing vendor relationships, and managing remote, cross-time-zone teams
Experience developing and presenting executive-level QBRs and improving stakeholder satisfaction
Proven ability to develop, train, and calibrate teams to a uniform standard
ERP experience (NetSuite preferred) plus a P2P platform such as Zip, Coupa, or Ariba
Bachelor’s in accounting, finance, business, or supply chain
Preferred: APM, CPSM, CPA, or equivalent
An ideal candidate also has:
The ability to solve complex problems with simple solutions
A history of being a collaborator, strategic thinker, and influencer
Experience scaling P2P operations in a high-growth, multi-entity, and multi-currency environment
Lean Six Sigma or similar process-improvement credentials, with automation and AI experience

title: Climate Program Manager
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
To avoid the worst effects of climate change, most climate models agree the world will need to dramatically reduce emissions and remove 5-10 billion tons of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere per year by 2050. The Climate team’s goal is to accelerate Stripe’s path to net zero in parallel with the world’s. We do this by reducing Stripe’s emissions and leading initiatives to increase the likelihood that we have the global carbon removal capacity necessary to reach these climate goals.
In 2019, we developed the first measurement of Stripe’s enterprise emissions. In 2021 we launched Stripe Climate , enabling merchants to direct a fraction of their revenue to help scale emerging carbon removal technologies. In 2022 we launched Frontier , an advance market commitment to buy $1.8B+ of permanent carbon removal by 2040. In 2024, we entered our first multi-year offtake for clean energy.
Today, Stripe’s corporate net zero program is entering a new phase. We are looking to streamline our emissions measurement, create a template for catalytic emission reduction and champion buying removals on the path to net zero, all while meeting our expanding global ESG disclosure requirements.
What you’ll do
As Stripe’s Climate Program Manager, you will set the strategy and lead the execution and reporting for Stripe’s corporate net zero program. You’ll partner with a wide range of stakeholders within and outside of Stripe – Accounting, Finance, Legal, Procurement, Facilities, Sales, and carbon accounting and assurance providers – to refine our greenhouse gas inventory, deliver a reduction and removal roadmap that meets our climate targets, and provide inputs to global ESG disclosures.
This role requires someone with expertise in carbon accounting and reductions strategy, sharp program and process management, a track record of getting big things done fast, and excellent judgement to make the ‘right’ recommendations for Stripe’s net zero program.
Responsibilities
Net Zero strategy (~15%): Own and evolve Stripe’s corporate net zero strategy, including Stripe’s transition plan, priorities, budget, annual goals, emissions forecasts, removal retirements, and progress tracking. Stay current on evolving disclosure requirements, net zero guidance, and industry best practices to ensure Stripe’s program is high impact and best in class
Emissions measurement (~30%): Build Stripe’s annual greenhouse gas inventory. Collect data inputs, evolve methodology, manage Stripe’s footprint vendors, run a rigorous and auditable process with cross-functional stakeholders, and identify opportunities to use AI to improve the accuracy and efficiency of this process
Emissions reporting (~30%):  Serve as Stripe’s subject-matter expert to deliver inputs to ESG controllership for regulatory disclosures and clear recommendations for executives and customers
Reduction program (~25%): Develop and manage emissions reduction initiatives across Stripe. This will include efforts like securing renewable electricity for Stripe’s scope 2 emissions, as well as driving creative and high-impact interventions like carbon removal or lower-emission data centers that we need to reach global net zero
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
BA or BS degree
5-7+ years of experience in corporate sustainability, climate strategy, carbon accounting, environmental consulting, or a related field
Excellent oral and written communication skills – especially adept at translating complexity into clear recommendations
A track record of generating and implementing ambitious emissions reduction initiatives
Strong quantitative skills and expertise in emissions accounting and Greenhouse Gas Protocol
Preferred qualifications
Has led a corporate climate program in a sector with a significant Scope 3 footprint, ideally technology or financial services
Is a self-starter, and has a proven track record of translating climate ambitions into actionable plans and producing measurable reductions through clean energy, cloud usage, and other supplier engagement initiatives
Has a working knowledge of major emissions accounting and climate reporting standards and requirements (e.g., CSRD, California SB 253, GHG protocol), and experience with Watershed or similar enterprise carbon management  platforms
Has experience partnering with cross functional controllership partners to manage a greenhouse gas inventory process that meets requirements for limited or reasonable assurance
Is an exceptionally fast learner. Enjoys (and has experience) quickly ramping on new reduction technologies and sustainability standards
